messages.subject: Introduction to Distance Sampling (fwd)
parts:
Apologies for advertising books on this list! Many of you will be
familiar with our book, 'Distance Sampling: Estimating Abundance of
Biological Populations', published by Chapman and Hall in 1993. Although
out-of-print with C&H, we have placed the book on our web pages
(http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distancebook/), and have printed extra
copies for those who wish to purchase it. We still receive orders
for the book, so members of the list may be interested to have an update
on plans to replace it.

'Introduction to Distance Sampling', by Steve Buckland, David Anderson,
Ken Burnham, Jeff Laake, David Borchers and Len Thomas, is due to be
published in July (UK) /August (USA) of this year by Oxford University
Press. It will cover most of the material of the 1993 book (though will
omit more advanced material). It will also have several new sections, and
the chapter on study design and field methods has been substantially
reworked and expanded. Details can be found at

http://www.oup.co.uk/isbn/0-19-850927-8 (paperback, UK site)
http://www.oup.co.uk/isbn/0-19-850649-X (hardback, UK site)
http://www.oup-usa.org/isbn/0198509278.html (paperback, US site)
http://www.oup-usa.org/isbn/019850649X.html (hardback, US site)

We are also working on a companion book, 'Advanced Distance Sampling',
which we hope will appear in 18 months or so.

Finally we are in the process of completing a book called 'Estimating
Animal Abundance: closed populations', by David Borchers, Steve
Buckland and Walter Zucchini, which will be published by Springer later
this year. It is intended to make the bewildering variety of abundance
estimation methods more accessible to the uninitiated and more coherent to
the cogniscenti. In it we emphasize the fundamental similarities of the
methods and draw out the common threads that underlie them. It covers all
commonly used methods for closed populations (including distance
sampling) from the simplest to the most advanced.

Steve Buckland
